T5 to Coordinator: both audit bugs are fixed in one PR, https://github.com/Zugzwang-world/graphpay/pull/104 (auto-merge on, CI pending; I'll report when it has merged). I have not seen the audit file (docs/plan/integration-audit.md is not on main yet), so I worked from your description and the code.
Cause of both: the graph returns a shop's OLDEST edges first and slices at the list cap without any flag. So the feed (limit 50) stopped showing new edges once its window held 50, and the CSV (limit 100) held only the October history (Kesar's incoming list at 100 ends on 24 Oct), with `truncated` never set.
Fix: both now ask for 500 rows per direction (the engine's own row cap, also passed as `listCap`), a full list or an engine-reported cap sets `truncated`, and a new `fetchShopEdgesFitting` shrinks the window (whole, half, ... today only) until the answer is whole. The CSV file name and `x-export-days` / `x-export-truncated` headers say how far back it reaches, the phone says so under Export, and the event stream sends a comment line if its window is ever full.
Read live from this Mac with the real code: stream window 60 edges, not truncated; CSV 295 rows from 6 Oct to 6 Nov 05:44 UTC (97 pay, 89 deliver, 4 refund, 99 order, plus renew/subscribe/fail rows), so the real payments are there. 177 web tests, typecheck, lint and `pnpm check` pass. It is read-only (nothing signs or spends), so no reviewer pass. One honest limit: past 500 rows per direction in a day the window shrinks to today only and then flags truncated; at today's volume (about 60 edges a day) that is far away.
</cross-session-message>
